notes: OpenRouter decision-model measurements, read from the server-rendered model pages and the rankings page on 2026-10-06 (all rows OpenRouter-measured, same method for every model). p50 latency is the best provider over all locations: a router-inclusive hosted round trip with undeclared payload mix, window 1 week (3 days for GPT-6 Luna Decisions). It is the best like-for-like hosted latency source found, and it ORDERS the models differently from the launch tables: Clef-flash 0.17 s < Jev 0.21 s < Perplexity 0.29 s < Clef 0.51 s (hosted Clef is slower than hosted Jev). Hosted Clef and Clef-flash run on Workers AI, which OpenRouter says truncates long text state to roughly the first 2K tokens. Per-endpoint latency_last_30m/throughput_last_30m fields in the API were null for every decision model. Prices and context are in the pricing and capability docs.

claims.statement: Hosted p50 on one measurement method (OpenRouter, 2026-10-06 pages): Clef-flash 0.17 s, Jev 0.21 s, Perplexity 0.29 s, Clef 0.51 s. Hosted Clef is about 2.4x SLOWER than hosted Jev here, the opposite of the Cloudflare launch ratio; Clef-flash is about 1.2x faster than Jev.
claims.implication: For a hosted hot path compare these like-for-like numbers, not the launch table. Re-measure from your own region with your own state size.

claims.statement: Outliers on the same page method: Kev 4B (SiliconFlow) p50 3.06 s and Solar Decide p50 17.30 s (second Upstage endpoint 19.58 s); not a hot-path latency for those routes at retrieval.

GPT-6 Luna Decisions on OpenRouter: p50 0.30 s (3-day window) and 3-day uptime 99.99% on the page in the capture (the endpoints API showed uptime_last_1d 100); the rankings page shows 343,958 weekly requests. JevBench independently measures 0.30 s adjusted.
